title: Scaling Deep Learning Training with MPMD Pipeline Parallelism
problem: GSPMD/SPMD-based pipeline parallelism in JAX can only encode GPipe-style schedules; it cannot express MPMD schedules like 1F1B or Interleaved 1F1B that improve memory efficiency and throughput, and it forces homogeneous stages with poor scalability over low-bandwidth (DCN) inter-node links.
motivation: The GPipe schedule stores all microbatch activations simultaneously (O(num_microbatches) memory), whereas 1F1B reduces this to O(num_stages). Best-practice LLM training (e.g., Llama-3) uses a mix of TP+PP+DP; SPMD encoding of PP in JAX cannot produce 1F1B or Interleaved 1F1B, leaving ~20% performance on the table due to extra rematerialization. DCN links between nodes have 10-100x lower bandwidth than NVLink/ICI, making PP with P2P communication essential at scale.
method: JaxPP lets you mark where one processing stage ends and another begins with simple annotations; it automatically infers the data flow between stages from your model code. Unlike systems that force a single execution pattern, JaxPP supports flexible gradient accumulation schedules—like 1F1B (one forward pass, one backward pass) and Interleaved 1F1B—that use memory more efficiently and improve throughput. A central controller orchestrates execution by converting your model to a task graph, distributing tasks to processing units (SPMD actors, each managing one or more devices), determining data movement through topological ordering to avoid deadlocks, freeing memory buffers once they're no longer needed, and bundling all data transfers into single efficient messages.
key_novelty: JaxPP is the first system that lets JAX users define any pipeline schedule they want—like 1F1B or Interleaved 1F1B—using simple code annotations, without requiring model rewrites.
contributions: MPMD runtime for JAX enabling arbitrary pipeline schedules decoupled from model implementation
pipeline_yield stage boundary annotation that is auto-differentiable and composes with JAX transforms
accumulate_grads API supporting 1F1B and Interleaved 1F1B schedules
Task graph runtime with topological send/receive inference, async P2P overlap, and buffer liveness pass
Loop commuting pass for efficient weight sharing (tied embeddings)
51.2% speedup over SPMD PP and 1.16x over JAX FSDP on GPT-3 175B (128 GPUs, H100)
98.33% weak scaling efficiency from 64 to 1024 H100 GPUs
95.6% throughput of NeMo's hand-optimized pipeline parallelism
hardware_target: NVIDIA H100 GPUs (DGX H100 nodes), InfiniBand NDR400 interconnect; multi-node clusters
limitations: Single-controller design introduces driver process as potential bottleneck at extreme scale
Dispatch overhead increases with many small stages; circular repeat must be tuned
No custom kernels except cuDNN attention; some NeMo optimizations (async TP, sequence parallelism) not included
